feed.title: epic-jam-2026 / devlog
feed.subtitle: A participant's devlog for the Epic AI MegaJam 2026

entry.title: builds.log
entry.summary: Every build of the jam so far, with the branches, features and fixes that went into it.

entry.title: day-4.log
entry.summary: One compile line, clothes on everyone, Shipping builds, a live playtest with 120 notes, and the submission.

entry.title: day-3.log
entry.summary: Build 1 starts. An escort, a cell with two cellmates who talk back through NVIDIA ACE, a kit-built castle and end credits. Then two GPU driver hangs, a hard reboot and a new way of working.

entry.title: day-2.log: builds, overload and one decision board
entry.summary: Five more packaged builds turned the prototype into a dense playable system. Day 2 also became a test of how to decide when agents, branches and boards move faster than one person can read.

entry.title: day-1.log: build the smallest world
entry.summary: At 06:00 there was no game. Eighteen hours later there was a tested UE 5.8 build ladder, an island, NPCs, time and weather, and an honest list of what was still broken.

entry.title: push_pull.md: inspiration, not a plan
entry.summary: There is no concept yet. There is a pile of directions pulling against each other, and me being overwhelmed at 3 AM, three hours before the start.

entry.title: validate.sh: the night before, and a Director's Cut
entry.summary: One long day of testing everything twice, an agent that went one step too far, deleting it all, the kickoff stream and the theme.

entry.title: boot.log: a kidnapped workstation
entry.summary: How a work PC got kidnapped twice before reaching the office, why I'm doing this at all, and the toolchain I set up in the two weeks before the jam.
